meta.purpose: Fire when the Risk Reasoning Agent finishes an assessment for a bridge, then invoke the Report Generation service entrypoint (G901) with that {bridge_id, cycle_id} scope. One document per finalized assessment. GLUE ONLY — contains NO document-building or judgment logic (Constitution III: modularity; n8n moves data, the Python service builds the document).  [n8n/Neon live verification deferred — none locally.]
meta.invokes: src/agents/report_generation/service.py :: run_report (exposed over HTTP by the report deployment) — one call per finalized assessment, per bridge
meta.assembly_logic: none — every part of building the document lives in the Python service (G901), never here; n8n only forwards the scope and routes on the structured ok flag
meta.mode: fire-and-notify (async) — the document build may take 5-30s, so this workflow does not block for it; the service runs the job and the completion signal is a separate downstream notification, not held open by n8n
meta.upstream: Risk Reasoning Agent assessment-available signal (Risk posts {bridge_id, cycle_id} to this webhook when its assessment for the bridge is persisted)
meta.out_of_scope: no distribution/submission of the document happens here — that is a separate downstream gated agent (FR-13); this workflow only kicks off document generation

nodes.name: Risk Assessment Available
nodes.notes: Fires when the Risk Reasoning Agent finishes an assessment for one bridge and posts {bridge_id, cycle_id}. No inspection of the assessment contents here — the scope is forwarded as-is.

nodes.name: Invoke Report Generation (G901)
nodes.notes: POST the {bridge_id, cycle_id} scope to the Python service entrypoint, which enqueues the job and returns quickly (fire-and-notify — n8n does not wait the full 5-30s). Retries the TRIGGER/invoke up to 3x on transport failure (Constitution IV: reliability). Redelivery is safe — the service is idempotent per assessment version (FR-10: supersede, not duplicate). The service returns a structured summary; n8n does not interpret its contents.

nodes.name: Job Accepted?
nodes.notes: Branch on the service's structured ok flag only — NEVER on the document's contents. Any routing on the outcome itself is downstream and out of scope for this glue workflow.

parameters.content: Job invocation failed at the service boundary (ok=false). Log + alert ops. The error detail is in {{ $json.error }}. No retry here — the HTTP node already retried transport; an ok=false is a structured result, not a transport fault.

Job accepted by the service (report_artifacts + decision_log will be written on completion). Nothing further for n8n to do here; the completion signal and any downstream distribution are separate workflows.
